references.text: Abraham fell on his face and laughed when God promised him a son with Sarah in their old age, which mirrors Sarah's laughter and unbelief when she heard the same promise.
Sarah says that God has given her reason for laughter, and all who hear it will laugh with her. The laughter has now turned to joy instead of doubt, and Isaac's name ('he laughs') reminds us of this.
Sarah is mentioned as an example of faith because she ultimately trusted that God was faithful and could fulfill his promise, despite her initial doubt and denial.
God knows the thoughts and words of all people. Sarah tried to deny her laughter, but the Lord knew the truth and confronted her with it.
